$comment: R1737 — WHERE A POINTER ARRIVES IN THE ANALYSIS TOOL'S SCREENS, and who
may be asked about it. Written down once, apart from the code that has to
satisfy it.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A RUST CONSTANT. The reason its siblings are. A
screen's own `spec` module is what a RUNNING screen needs, and a
specification written there is written by the same hand that has to satisfy
it — so the gate ends up asking the thing under test for the right answer
(R1728). This file is the other hand. It is tracked, it is read by the demo,
and the demo may not edit it to pass.
WHAT OPENED IT. R1736 repaired a one-pixel defect: a screen was told the
pixel BEFORE the one the pointer was over, at some coordinates and not
others, because the router hands a fraction and the surface multiplies it
back. A press carries no position of its own — it acts on the cursor the
last move recorded — so the whole screen was aimed wrong by that much, and
a person reported it as 'sometimes the node is selected and sometimes the
background behind it is'.
That repair was measured by walking a real pointer over 600 columns and 600
rows of a running screen and asking the screen where it thought the pointer
was. MEASURED HERE, at the start of this round: of the five screens in this
tree that hit-test themselves, three publish a cursor field — in TWO
incompatible spellings, an `"x,y"` string and an `{x, y}` object — and TWO
publish nothing at all. So the check that found the defect could not be run
on two of the five, and on the other three it depended on each screen's own
vocabulary.
The fact was never the screen's to volunteer. The framework resolves the
reading, and at that moment holds both accounts of where the pointer is.
The vocabulary here is neutral by requirement: this describes the analysis
tool's screens, not any particular product's.
THE ARRIVAL IS ASKABLE FOR EVERY SURFACE, WITHOUT THE SURFACE SAYING
ANYTHING.
The population is the scene's painted surfaces and not the arrival store,
and that direction is what makes the census honest: a report built by
walking what the store holds could only list surfaces a pointer already
reached, so 'no surface drifted' would be satisfied by a run that pointed
at nothing.
THE FLOOR, MEASURED by building a probe at 6.11.1 and running it. There
an outside observer CAN ask, for any widget, where the pointer is in that
widget's own frame, without the widget having stored anything — exact
over 400 columns and 300 rows of a child widget, no misses. Universality
was the floor's and this tree owed it. This surface is the debt paid.

canon.title: every painted surface has an arrival row, whatever it publishes
a surface no pointer reached is named, not counted as clean
and the answer has the same shape on every screen

$comment: THE FRAMEWORK COMPARES THE TWO ACCOUNTS IT HOLDS, AND PUBLISHES THE
VERDICT.
At the moment it resolves a reading the framework has the cursor the
window system reported and the rectangle the fraction is taken over. The
pixel the pointer is over is `floor(cursor) - rect.origin`, arithmetic
with no fraction in it; the pixel the surface will resolve is
`pixel_of(fraction, extent)`. Two derivations of one fact.
Three verdicts, and only one is a defect. `strayed` is a capture lock
forwarding past the rectangle's edge on purpose, where the resolved pixel
is a clamp and not a claim — folding it into either neighbour would
either manufacture a defect or hide one.
THE FLOOR, MEASURED. It never compares its own two accounts, and its
answer is not this question at all: it reports WHERE THE CURSOR IS, not
where the event ARRIVED. A press delivered to a child at (37, 21),
followed by moving the cursor, leaves it answering (300, 250). Across the
five types such a record could live on there are 245 declared properties
and 195 declared methods; 3 are point-typed, all of them the widget's own
position in its parent, and 0 methods return a point. None is a delivered
position, and for a synthesised event the position it carried is
unreadable.

canon.title: the pixel a surface is told is the pixel the pointer was over
two pixels of the same rectangle is a defect, and says which way
a cursor outside the rectangle is a clamp, not a disagreement

$comment: AND IT HOLDS ON EVERY SCREEN THAT HIT-TESTS ITSELF, swept with the
machine's own pointer.
Stated per-pixel and not per-control on purpose: which pixels a
truncating multiplication loses depends on the extent, so any list of
points somebody chooses can miss them all — which is exactly how R1736's
defect survived every gate in this tree.
The population is the five screens that implement a hit test of their
own, counted rather than assumed. R1736 repaired one of them and measured
two; the other two could not be measured at all, which is what this round
changed.

canon.title: every column of the surface arrives as itself
every row of the surface arrives as itself
on all five screens that resolve a press themselves

$comment: IT IS WHERE THE EVENT ARRIVED, NOT WHERE THE CURSOR HAPPENS TO BE.
The distinction the floor cannot draw, and the reason the record is
written at the delivery rather than read from a live cursor. It also
settles what may write it: a READ must not move it. R1736's own lesson is
that a probe which disturbs what it measures measures the disturbance —
its first reproduction table was its own drag drift — and a census that
recorded an arrival while answering 'what would a wheel here do' would be
that same mistake built into the framework.

canon.title: the record is the last delivery, and it does not follow the cursor
asking the census leaves the record where it was

owed.sentence: while a router drag session runs, the position arrives over a drop target's rectangle and no arrival is recorded
why: A router with a session open stops calling `pointer_move` and sends
the position as a drop point whose fraction is taken over the
resolved DROP TARGET's rectangle — which is in general not the
surface's own, and whose tag is not the surface's tag. So both halves
of this record would mean something different there: a different key
and a different comparison. Stated rather than papered over, because
the honest consequence is that the arrival goes stale for the
duration of a drag.

owed.sentence: the wheel and two-finger channels record no arrival
why: They normalise over a possibly different basis and their consumers
read the FRACTION — a notch does not resize what it is measured over.
The pixel a fraction names is not a quantity they compute, so a
landing verdict for them would be a judgement on arithmetic that
never runs. A wheel-only surface therefore reads as `never`, which is
true of the record and worth knowing.

owed.sentence: the arrivals of a surface that leaves the screen are forgotten, drifts included
why: A surface no longer painted has its size, its painted regions and now
its arrivals dropped, so it cannot answer where a pointer is and a
different screen reusing the tag cannot inherit its position. The
cost is that a drift on a page navigated away from is forgotten with
the page, so the check covers the surfaces a run ended with. The
alternative — a store that grows without bound and answers for things
that are gone — is worse, and the honest fix is not a longer memory
but a report that says what it dropped. Stated here rather than
papered over because a gate's coverage is exactly the thing this
round found itself getting wrong twice.
